Write a complete OpenFOAM case for a 2D lid-driven cavity flow using the icoFoam solver.
The domain is a square cavity of side length 0.1 m, extruded 0.01 m in the z-direction, giving a thin 2D slab.
The mesh is a uniform Cartesian grid of 20×20×1 cells, generated with blockMesh.
The blockMeshDict defines 8 vertices: (0 0 0), (0.1 0 0), (0.1 0.1 0), (0 0.1 0), (0 0 0.01), (0.1 0 0.01), (0.1 0.1 0.01), (0 0.1 0.01), with a single block of 20 20 1 cells and a simpleGrading of 1 1 1.
The blockMeshDict defines four boundary patches: movingWall on the top face (y = 0.1), fixedWalls on the left (x = 0), right (x = 0.1), and bottom (y = 0) faces, and frontAndBack on the two z-faces (z = 0 and z = 0.01).
The fluid is incompressible with a kinematic viscosity nu of 0.001 m²/s, specified in system/transportProperties.
The lid velocity is 1 m/s in the x-direction, applied as fixedValue uniform (1 0 0) on the movingWall patch.
The velocity boundary conditions in 0/U are: movingWall uses fixedValue uniform (1 0 0), fixedWalls uses noSlip, and frontAndBack uses empty.
The pressure boundary conditions in 0/p are: movingWall uses zeroGradient, fixedWalls uses zeroGradient, and frontAndBack uses empty.
The initial velocity field in 0/U is uniform (0 0 0).
The initial pressure field in 0/p is uniform 0.
The controlDict sets startTime to 0, endTime to 0.5, deltaT to 0.002, writeControl to timeStep, and writeInterval to 20, giving 250 total time steps with output every 20th step.
The fvSchemes file uses the standard icoFoam defaults: ddtSchemes Euler, gradSchemes Gauss linear, divSchemes bounded Gauss linearUpwind grad(U), laplacianSchemes Gauss linear corrected, interpolationSchemes linear, snGradSchemes corrected.
The fvSolution file uses smoothSolver with GAMG preconditioner for U, GAMG for p, PISO with nCorrectors 2 and nNonOrthogonalCorrectors 0, and SIMPLE with nNonOrthogonalCorrectors 0.
The case directory structure includes system/, 0/, and constant/ folders, with all files placed in their correct locations.
The Reynolds number of the flow is 100, computed as Re = U*L/nu = 1 * 0.1 / 0.001.
